header.running_head: The fervour that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) had to Spend in the Path of Allaah

Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "You will have to prove what you are saying." "Certainly," responded Hadhrat Ali (RA), "By Allaah, I can certainly prove myself. Do you recall the time when Rasulullaah ﷺ sent you to collect Zakaah? Remember when you approached Abbaas bin Abdil Muttalib (RA) and he refused to pay his Zakaah to you because there had been a problem between you and him? You then told me to accompany you to Rasulullaah ﷺ to inform him about what Abbaas (RA) did. We then went to Rasulullaah ﷺ but returned because we discovered that he was feeling very cheerless. We then went back to him the following morning and when we found him in a cheerful mood, I informed him about what Abbaas (RA) had done. He then said to you, 'Do you not realise that a person's paternal uncle is like his father?'
We then mentioned to Rasulullaah ﷺ that we had found him to be cheerless on the first day but again happy on the second. He said to us, "When you came on the first day, I still had with me two Dinaars of Sadaqah funds left over and it was this that caused me to in that mood (because I was worried that I should not die with it in my possession). However, when you came on the second day, I had already spent it and that had put me in the good mood that you saw."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "You are right. I am grateful to you for the first thing you told me (about changing conviction to assumption) and for the second thing (reminding me of the incident)." [^1]
The Incident between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) Concerning the Distribution of some wealth

Hadhrat Talha bin Ubaydullaah (RA) reports that some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and he duly distributed it amongst the people. When some of it was left over, he consulted with the people about what to do with it. They said, "You should keep it for any needs that may arise." Hadhrat Ali (RA) who was also present there, remained silent without expressing any opinion. Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "What is the matter, O Abul Hasan? Why are you not saying anything?" "The people have already spoken," replied Hadhrat Ali (RA). When Hadhrat Umar (RA) insisted that Hadhrat Ali (RA) voice his opinion, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "Allaah has already distributed this wealth (by detailing the recipients in the Qur'aan. The remaining amount should also be distributed likewise)." Hadhrat Ali (RA) then proceeded to mention the incident when wealth arrived from Bahrain and Rasulullaah ﷺ had not yet distributed all of it when nightfall prevented him from completing.
